fix: Append a compact, XML-tagged <deliverable-contract> block to the tail of every contracted phase's dispatch prompt: exact artifact path, required section headings verbatim, and the rendered sentinel template (reuse phasecontract's ONE template source so writer/detector cannot drift — the existing no-drift pin covers it). Keep the persona body's narrative guidance; the tail block is the machine contract restated adjacent to generation. MEASURE: contract-block rate per phase per 20 cycles before/after (the data already lands in the cycle logs). Do NOT also duplicate it a third time — one persona mention + one tail block.
notes: From the 2026-07-30 LLM-stability review. Companion to contract-block-cli-escalation (the compensating control when a CLI ignores the contract regardless of placement).
summary: Anthropic's own guidance: Claude follows instructions in the USER TURN better than in the system message, and XML-tagged sections parse unambiguously. Our required-sections list + machine-verdict sentinel template live in the persona body (system-ish, far from the generation point) — yet the CORRECTION prompt, which puts the exact same requirements in the turn tail, is what gets compliance. That asymmetry is a free experiment with a measurable outcome: the contract-block rate per phase.
title: Move hard deliverable-contract requirements to the GENERATION POINT (turn tail), not the persona body
consumed_by: console-2026-07-30: LANDED — PR #383 squash 9574e66c. phasecontract.RenderContractTail() emits the <deliverable-contract> XML block at the point the prompt is generated, so requirements travel with the request instead of living only in a persona file the agent may not re-read. Review HIGH fixed in the same PR: when RequireFailureContext is set the exemplar must itself be failure-bearing, or the agent is shown a passing example for a requirement about failures. selfCheckCommand() single-sourced so the block and the persona cannot disagree.
